children: BlackRock
CEO Larry Fink is warning that delays in building data centers could do more than slow the artificial intelligence boom. They could also
keep computing costs elevated, add to inflation pressure and weaken economic growth

If we don't build out these data centers, it is actually more inflationary because the cost of compute is so high right now, Fink said in an interview with Bloomberg Television at the Berlin Global Dialogue.
His argument is essentially a supply story.
AI demand is rising rapidly, but computing capacity remains constrained. If data center construction slows, that shortage could keep the price of compute high for businesses trying to deploy AI.
The faster we can build out more data centers, the more compute we have, the faster we can bring down the cost, Fink said.
He went further, warning that slowing the buildout of AI infrastructure could jeopardize the economy.

That matters for a broad group of companies tied to the expansion, including Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, Equinix, Digital Realty, Vertiv and other chip, cloud, power and data center infrastructure providers.
But there is a problem.
The amount of capital required to finance AI infrastructure is enormous, and the cost of that capital is rising.
Fink said competition for private capital is as intense as he has seen during his career.
At the same time, higher Treasury yields are creating another layer of pressure.
Fink pointed to the nearly
$2 trillion U.S. federal budget deficit
, arguing that the bond market is effectively warning Washington that persistent deficits are becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.
Investor Takeaway
I think Fink's warning highlights a growing contradiction inside the AI boom.
The industry needs
massive investment to bring down the cost of compute
, but higher interest rates and rising bond yields make that investment more expensive.
That creates a potential feedback loop.

If financing costs delay data centers, compute supply stays constrained. If compute remains scarce, AI deployment becomes more expensive, potentially limiting the productivity gains investors are counting on.
For investors, the key things to watch are
data center construction timelines, electricity availability, financing costs, Treasury yields and whether compute prices begin falling as new capacity comes online
The AI story is increasingly becoming an infrastructure story.
And according to Fink, failing to build that infrastructure quickly enough could become an economic problem, not just a technology problem.

title: BlackRock CEO Sees Trouble Brewing in $1 Trillion AI Boom
